title: Keep design-system files from importing app or wagon code

facts.note: Any file under a design root (directory named design, design_system or design-system); the source sets no file-kind or language restriction. Repos with no design root are not judged.

Static import scan of the file (existing or newly added imports alike) that resolves each relative / design-directory-alias specifier and checks whether the target leaves the file's containing design root (statement) — the term definition says 'outside every design root'; see verifier_detail for this unresolved source tension.

fires: A file under a design root adds a relative import like ../../app/... or ../../wagons/... that resolves outside the design root.
A file under a design root already contains (unchanged) a relative import that resolves into app or wagon code.
A design-owned .ts file under a design root imports a type or constant from a wagon via a relative path.
A design-system file imports via an alias that names a design directory but resolves to app or wagon code.

A file under one design root imports a relative path that leaves its containing design root (statement wording); note the term definition 'outside every design root' would not flag it if the target is inside another design root — source tension, needs canonical clarification.
doesNotFire: The repository has no directory named design, design_system or design-system.
App or wagon code imports from the design system (the allowed direction).
A design-system file imports a bare package specifier such as `hono/jsx`.
A test file (*.test.*, *.spec.*) or a file in a vendored/build directory under the design root imports outward.
A design-system file uses an alias that does not name a design directory.
A relative import whose target stays inside the importing file's own design root.

given: A file under a design root (directory named `design`, `design_system` or `design-system`)
then: The import MUST NOT resolve outside the file's design root; the design system stays independent of app and wagon code.
prefer: Pass app-specific values into design components, or move genuinely shared, design-owned types/constants inward.
During GREEN: use props or existing design-system contracts for the current value.
During GREEN: add only the smallest input surface the acceptance requires.
During GREEN: move a type or constant only when it is truly owned by the design system.
avoid: Importing a wagon through a barrel or alias.
Relocating app-specific concepts into design code just to make the import legal.
Broadening the fix by generalizing unrelated design APIs.
unless: Test files (`*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`) and vendored/build directories are never scanned.
Bare package specifiers (`hono/jsx`) are outside the project graph; not judged.
Aliased specifiers are judged only when they name a design directory.
A repository with no design root is not judged: no system to connect to yet.
why: Wagons and app code import FROM the design system, never the reverse, keeping it wagon-agnostic; a system reaching into a wagon becomes part of it, can't be reused by the next one, and breaks when the wagon changes.
evidence: bun_design_system_detector reports no outward_import for any file under a design root.
Design-system files import nothing from app or wagon code.
The current behavioral or rendering acceptance passes.
verifier_detail: The first directory beneath a design root names the layer: `tokens` or `foundations`, `primitives`, `components`, `templates`.

outward_import (term definition): a relative import from a design-system file whose target lies outside every design root. Detector summary: flags relative imports from a design-system file that leave the design root.

Source tension (unresolved, needs canonical clarification): the statement forbids relative imports resolving outside 'the design root' (the containing root), while the outward_import term says 'outside every design root'. A relative import from one design root into a different design root violates the statement but not the term definition. The coder-facing rule keeps the statement's stricter containing-root boundary; do not treat cross-root imports as exempt.
Self-scoping: if no design root exists, the rule does not judge the repository.
Exclusions: *.test.*, *.spec.*, vendored/build directories never scanned; bare package specifiers (`hono/jsx`) not judged; aliased specifiers judged only when they name a design directory.

Scope: the canonical rule covers every file under a design root and every relative import in it (existing or newly added). graph.json reports the current detector scanning .tsx/.jsx/.html/.css; that is a detector coverage limit, not a narrowing of the rule — files of other kinds (e.g. .ts) remain in scope.
audit: Bun realization of the outward half of `coder.design.hierarchy-import`, mirroring `coder.vite.design-wagons-import`.
Open question for canonical owners: containing-root (statement) vs every-root (term) boundary for outward_import.

sharedNodes.text: During GREEN make only the smallest change the current acceptance requires. Prove: the current behavioral or rendering acceptance passes.

additions.text: Explicit note of the containing-root vs every-root tension between the statement and the outward_import term; coder-facing then follows the statement's containing-root boundary.
additions.justification: The source is internally inconsistent; the tension is exposed rather than silently resolved, and the stricter statement wording is kept so S006 is not weakened.

additions.text: Note that graph.json's detector file-kind list (.tsx/.jsx/.html/.css) is a coverage limit, not a rule scope.
additions.justification: Preserves the broader canonical scope while recording the known detector limitation from graph context.

additions.text: Coder-facing text kept slightly above ~1,000 chars.
additions.justification: The phase-independent canonical alternative and the GREEN-qualified entries must both be kept; losslessness wins over brevity.

trace.note: Containing-root boundary kept; tension with S014 recorded.
Term id kept; definition placed in verifier_detail.
'During GREEN' qualifier attached to each GREEN-specific prefer entry.
Heading function carried by the avoid list ('Broadening...' in avoid[2]).
